title: Protocol for fever-range whole-body hyperthermia (WBH) in mice to study febrile effect on T-cell adhesion and migration
protocol: Inject C57BL/6J mice intraperitoneally with 1 mL sterile 0.9% saline.
Place mice in an environmental chamber pre-set at 38.8°C for 6 h to achieve fever-range whole-body hyperthermia (core temperature 39.5 ± 0.5°C).
Maintain normothermia control mice at 22°C for the experimental period to keep core temperature 36.8 ± 0.2°C.
Sacrifice WBH or normothermia treated mice by CO2.
Disrupt spleen in PBS containing 2% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Pass cell suspension through a 70 μm mesh nylon strainer to remove aggregates and debris.
Centrifuge sample at 300 × g for 10 minutes.
Resuspend cells at a concentration of 1 × 10^8 nucleated cells/mL in 1 mL PBS in a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 50 μL Rat Serum to the sample and transfer it to a 5 mL polystyrene round-bottom tube.
Add 50 μL Isolation Cocktail to the sample.
Mix and incubate at 20°C–25°C for 10 minutes.
Vortex RapidSpheresTM for 30 seconds before use to ensure even dispersion.
Add 75 μL of RapidSpheresTM to the sample, mix thoroughly, and incubate at 20°C–25°C for 2.5 minutes.
Add 1.5 mL PBS to top up the sample, mix by gently pipetting up and down 2–3 times.
Place the tube into the magnet and incubate at 20°C–25°C for 2.5 minutes.
Pick up the magnet and in one continuous motion invert the magnet and tube, pouring the enriched cell suspension into a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Leave the magnet and tube inverted for 2–3 seconds before returning upright without shaking or blotting off any drops that may remain hanging from the mouth of the tube.
Wash the spot with blocking buffer.
Coat the polystyrene petri dish with 20 μL blocking buffer for 1 hour at 37°C.
Aspirate off the blocking buffer.
Cover the coated protein on the polystyrene petri dish with a silicon rubber gasket.
Cover the gasket with a flow chamber deck and assemble the flow system apparatus connecting inlet, outlet, and vacuum lines to the deck.
Fill the system with media and remove all air from the system.
Wash isolated T cells twice using washing buffer to eliminate free metal ions.
Collect washed T cells by centrifugation at 750 × g for 7 minutes.
Wash the collected T cells twice using buffer A to clear away EDTA in washing buffer.
Collect T cells again by centrifugation at 750 × g for 7 minutes.
Dilute the collected T cells to 1 × 10^6/mL in buffer A containing 1 mM Ca2+ + Mg2+ immediately before infusion.
Infuse diluted T cells into flow chamber at a consistent shear stress of 1 dyn/cm² for 1 minute using a syringe pump.
Pre-treat cells with 10 μg/mL α4β7 blocking antibody DATK32 when examining α4β1-mediated cell adhesion on VCAM-1 substrate.
Test the affinity of VCAM-1 to integrin α4β1 and MAdCAM-1 to integrin α4β7 in advance.
Wash the chamber with 1–2 mL washing buffer if there are too many non-specific T cells adherent to the surface of the polystyrene petri dish.
Monitor the motion of each adherent cell for 10 s following the initial adhesion point.
Define rolling adhesion as cells exhibiting rolling motions ≥ 5 s with a velocity of at least 1 μm/s.
Define firm adhesion as cells remaining adherent and stationary for at least 10 s.
Coat both sides of transwell chambers with 5 μg/mL mouse VCAM-1-Fc or MAdCAM-1-Fc.
Add T cells (2 × 10^6/mL in 150 μL RPMI 1640 medium) to the upper chamber.
Fill the lower chamber with 600 μL RPMI 1640 medium containing CCL21 (500 ng/mL).
Incubate cells at 37°C for 4 hours in 5% CO2.
Scrape cells remaining on the upper surface of the chamber with a cotton swab.
Fix cells that have migrated to the bottom surface with 2% formaldehyde at 20°C–25°C for 10 minutes.
Stain fixed cells with DAPI at 20°C–25°C for 10 minutes.
Enumerate stained cells by fluorescence microscope.
Alternatively, stain migrated cells with 0.5% Crystal Violet and enumerate them by microscope.
Pre-treat cells with 10 μg/mL α4β7 blocking antibody DATK32 when examining α4β1-mediated cell transmigration across VCAM-1 substrate.
